what: The query encoder's in-app memory footprint under Metal, macOS. Plan-of-record A-2 — the measurement half of B-4. The CPU shape (iPhone-16e simulator) and the CLI ceiling were already known; this is the third and last point.
harness: FRUSExplorer/App/SemanticEncoderFootprintRunner.swift, DEBUG-only, armed by FRUS_ENCODER_FOOTPRINT. Samples task_vm_info phys_footprint/resident_size at four points: before, after load, after 25 encodes, after unload (+2 s settle).
platform: macOS 26.6.2 (25G83), 10 active processors, n_gpu_layers default -1 (all layers)
reproduce: Launch with `open -n --env FRUS_ENCODER_FOOTPRINT=1 -a <app>`, NOT by running the binary from a shell. A shell-launched app is never frontmost, App Nap throttles the runner's .utility detached Task, and the run takes ~116 s instead of ~10 s (three attempts produced no JSON at all inside a 150 s window). Run 1 below was taken that way; its three encoder points agree with the rest and only its BASELINE is high, which is what App Nap leaves resident.

runs.launch: shell (App Nap throttled; JSON after ~116 s)

readings: Peak footprint is ~301 MB and the post-unload floor ~141 MB, so the encoder costs about 160 MB of footprint while loaded.
It releases COMPLETELY: the fourth point lands 6 MB BELOW the run's own baseline (mean 141.4 against 147.8). The plan's CPU-shape claim holds under Metal.

Metal peaks ~91 MB LOWER than the CPU shape (301 vs 393), because the GGUF is mmapped and its clean pages are resident without being charged to phys_footprint — visible in the resident column, which peaks ~645 MB against a 229 MB model file.
Both are far under the CLI ceiling (639 MB footprint / 861 MB peak RSS), as the spike said a ceiling should be.
Load-on-demand plus unload is comfortable at the 3 GB iPadOS floor: the cost is transient and fully returned.
